title: A threshold that follows the pool

blocks.text: The page's threshold heuristic is **`N / (parallelism * 4)` with a minimum**: enough tasks for good load balancing without the overhead of tiny ones. Its Q1 reads the parallelism from the pool and takes `Math.max(minimum, N / (parallelism * 4))`.
Write `AdaptiveSum.sum(pool, array, floor, probe)`: it sums `array` with a `RecursiveTask` **run in `pool`**, whose threshold is

A range of at most that many elements is summed sequentially; a longer one is split at the midpoint into two subtasks. In each base case, call `probe.leaf(start, end)` once. Values may be as large as a `long` allows, as may the sum.

cases.says: For a large array the threshold is N / (parallelism * 4), read from the given pool.
When N / (parallelism * 4) is below the floor, the floor is the threshold.
Every leaf runs in the pool that was passed in, not in the common pool.
Values of 3 and 4 billion sum to 6,999,999,999 with -1: each leaf sums in a long.

concepts: A threshold of N / (parallelism * 4), with a minimum, gives enough tasks for load balancing without tiny ones.
